research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; CSEW missing-value and rounding conventions, panel attrition, transferred or cancelled records, prepublication verification and open-data editioning; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW missing-answer convention
verified_claims: CSEW analysis generally excludes don't-know responses
refusals are also excluded unless otherwise specified
table bases therefore depend on valid responses
limitations: excluded missing responses are not negative answers
item-specific exceptions must be read from the table notes

sources.name: CSEW incident rounding convention
verified_claims: published CSEW incident estimates are rounded to the nearest 1,000
percentages and rates use separate presentation conventions
rounded totals may not reproduce calculations from unrounded data
limitations: rounded incident counts must not be treated as exact observations
derived rates should use official unrounded inputs where available

sources.name: CSEW panel-test response context
verified_claims: CSEW response was 46 percent in years ending March 2024 and March 2025
pre-pandemic response averaged around 70 percent
ONS evaluated panel feasibility against this declining-response context
limitations: response rate alone does not determine bias
period comparisons require consistent calculation rules

sources.name: CSEW experimental panel follow-up design
verified_claims: the main survey supplied the first experimental panel wave
respondents agreeing to recontact were followed by telephone
follow-up waves occurred approximately one year apart
limitations: mode changes can create panel and modal effects
the experimental design is not interchangeable with the standard cross-sectional series

sources.name: CSEW panel attrition risk
verified_claims: cumulative response declined across panel waves
attrition was unlikely to be random
some demographic and socioeconomic groups were less likely to remain
limitations: attrition effects differ by outcome and group
panel estimates require wave-specific response evidence

sources.name: Panel weighting limitation
verified_claims: weighting can adjust known population characteristics
selective attrition reduces the scope for correction
weighting cannot fully correct unobserved or behaviourally driven responder differences
limitations: weighted panel results retain representativeness uncertainty
known-control balance does not prove unbiased crime estimates

sources.name: Transferred and cancelled crime-record methodology
verified_claims: transferred or cancelled records were formerly called no-crimes
since April 2015 forces have supplied five reason categories
records can be transferred to another force or cancelled after additional information
limitations: reason categories require publication-year definitions
transferred and cancelled records are not outcome successes or failures

sources.name: Transferred and cancelled population boundary
verified_claims: the transferred or cancelled series begins with records initially recorded as crimes
incidents never recorded as crimes are outside the series
the measure therefore does not describe all non-recording decisions
limitations: absence from the series is not proof that no incident occurred
recording and cancellation stages must remain separate

sources.name: Crime outcomes prepublication verification
verified_claims: Home Office statisticians quality assure monthly crime and outcome data
before publication data are returned to every force for verification
forces can confirm or resubmit data when inconsistencies are identified
limitations: force confirmation is not an independent record-level audit
later revisions remain possible

sources.name: Crime outcomes open-data edition contract
verified_claims: the open-data page lists a year-ending March 2026 outcomes workbook
separate annual workbooks are retained for prior years
a separate historical ODS covers year ending March 2006 through year ending March 2014
limitations: file format and schema vary across editions
cross-year analysis requires explicit edition and field mapping
